questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: In the opening blood-picture table on p77, what is the baseline blood picture of iron deficiency anemia?
questions.exp: The p77 table lists the baseline blood picture of iron deficiency anemia as normocytic normochromic. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: When does iron deficiency anemia show a microcytic hypochromic blood picture according to the p77 table?
opts: Only when complicated by rheumatoid arthritis
Before serum ferritin begins to fall
In Stage I pre-latent negative iron balance
questions.exp: Iron deficiency anemia is normocytic normochromic (microcytic hypochromic in severe anemia). (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: According to the p77 table, anemia of chronic disease typically presents with which blood picture?
opts: Uniformly microcytic hypochromic in every etiology
questions.exp: Anemia of chronic disease has a normocytic normochromic blood picture in most cases. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: Which two exceptions in anemia of chronic disease are specifically noted to produce a microcytic hypochromic blood picture?
opts: Chronic kidney disease and ulcerative colitis
questions.exp: The p77 table notes that anemia of chronic disease is normocytic normochromic except in rheumatoid arthritis and miliary TB (microcytic hypochromic). (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: The blood picture of sideroblastic anemia in the p77 comparison table is ____ (microcytic, macrocytic).
questions.exp: Sideroblastic anemia is listed with a dimorphic (microcytic, macrocytic) blood picture. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: In the opening table, the blood picture of thalassemia trait (minor) is:
questions.exp: Thalassemia trait (minor) is listed as microcytic hypochromic. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: Match each anemia to its characteristic blood picture in the opening table — 1) Iron deficiency anemia 2) Anemia of chronic disease 3) Sideroblastic anemia 4) Thalassemia trait (minor) … A) Dimorphic (microcytic, macrocytic) B) Microcytic hypochromic C) Normocytic normochromic (microcytic hypochromic in severe anemia) D) Normocytic normochromic except in rheumatoid arthritis and miliary TB
questions.exp: IDA is normocytic normochromic (microcytic hypochromic in severe anemia); ACD is normocytic normochromic except RA and miliary TB; sideroblastic anemia is dimorphic; thalassemia trait is microcytic hypochromic. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: Chemically, hepcidin is classified in the pathophysiology section as a:
questions.exp: Hepcidin is described as a peptide hormone. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: Hepcidin is a peptide hormone produced in the ____.
questions.exp: Hepcidin is produced in the liver. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: In normal physiology on p77, stimulation of hepcidin acts directly on which transporter?
questions.exp: Physiology: Stimulation of hepcidin → Regulates ferroportin. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: When hepcidin regulates ferroportin in normal physiology, what is the downstream effect on iron?
opts: Decreased release of Fe²⁺ into circulation
Direct uptake of transferrin-bound iron into erythroblasts
Enhanced oxidation of Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺ at the brush border
Increased export of Fe³⁺ from duodenal enterocytes into plasma
questions.exp: Physiology: Stimulation of hepcidin → Regulates ferroportin → ↓ release of Fe2+ into circulation. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: In the pathology of anemia of chronic disease, marked inflammation causes increased release of ____.
questions.exp: Pathology flowchart: ↑↑ Inflammation → ↑↑ release of IL-6, activin. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: In the ACD pathology cascade, increased release of IL-6 and activin leads to increased stimulation of hepcidin synthesis, which then acts to:
questions.exp: ↑↑ release of IL-6, activin → ↑↑ stimulation of hepcidin synthesis → Inhibit ferroportin. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: When ferroportin is inhibited in anemia of chronic disease, iron becomes trapped in which three storage sites?
opts: Circulating reticulocytes, plasma and lymph nodes
Gastric parietal cells, pancreas and thyroid
Renal cortex, bone matrix and skeletal muscle
questions.exp: Inhibit ferroportin → Iron trapped in the stores (Duodenal cells, liver, spleen). (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: A patient with chronic inflammatory disease has high IL-6 and activin levels that stimulate hepatic hepcidin and trap iron inside duodenal cells, liver, and spleen. What is the resulting final state in the p77 pathology flowchart?
opts: Increased release of iron from macrophages into plasma
Systemic iron overload with saturated plasma transferrin
Excessive unbound ferrous iron in the portal vein
questions.exp: The pathology cascade ends with iron trapped in stores (duodenal cells, liver, spleen) → Deficient iron in circulation. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: How does hypoxia regulate hepcidin and intestinal iron absorption on p77?
opts: Hypoxia inhibits ferroportin directly → traps iron in enterocytes → decreased iron absorption
Hypoxia stimulates hepcidin → degrades ferroportin → decreased iron absorption
Hypoxia stimulates HFE and Tfr2 → increases hepcidin → prevents iron overload
Hypoxia inhibits hepcidin → no regulation of ferroportin → increased iron absorption
questions.exp: Factors regulating hepcidin: Hypoxia → inhibits hepcidin → no regulation of ferroportin → ↑ iron absorption. (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: The HFE gene that regulates hepcidin is located on which chromosome?
questions.exp: The p77 note specifies HFE gene (chromosome 6). (Book p77)

questions.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
questions.q: How do the HFE gene (chromosome 6), hemojuvelin, and Tfr2 regulate hepcidin and iron balance?
opts: They inhibit hepcidin → increased iron absorption → promote erythropoiesis
They block transferrin binding → increased urinary iron clearance
They degrade ferroportin directly → increased iron excretion in bile
They stimulate hepcidin → decreased iron absorption → prevent iron overload
questions.exp: HFE gene (chromosome 6), hemojuvelin, Tfr2 → stimulates hepcidin → ↓ iron absorption → Prevent iron overload. (Book p77)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: According to the note at the top of p78, an HFE gene mutation leads to ____.
questions.exp: Note on p78: HFE gene mutation → Hemochromatosis. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Besides regulating duodenal absorption, hepcidin is noted on p78 to play a role in recycling iron from which three cell types?
opts: Podocytes, renal tubular cells and astrocytes
questions.exp: Note on p78: Hepcidin also plays a role in recycling iron from macrophages, enterocytes & hepatocytes. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: In the blood indices for anemia of chronic disease (p78), serum ferritin is:

questions.q: In the blood indices for anemia of chronic disease (p78), serum iron is:

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: In the blood indices for anemia of chronic disease (p78), Total Iron Binding Capacity (TIBC) is:
questions.exp: Blood indices in ACD: TIBC (Total iron binding capacity) : Low. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Why is TIBC low in anemia of chronic disease according to the parenthetical note on p78?
opts: Transferrin is rapidly lost through glomerular filtration
Unbound protoporphyrin directly chelates circulating transferrin
Depleted marrow stores trigger compensatory transferrin degradation
Iron stores are adequate, leading to less transferrin synthesis
questions.exp: TIBC is Low (Store adequate → less transferrin synthesis). (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Which formula is printed beneath Transferrin saturation in the blood indices list on p78?
questions.exp: Transferrin saturation formula on p78: (Sr. iron / TIBC) × 100. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: What is the level of transferrin saturation in anemia of chronic disease on p78?
questions.exp: Transferrin saturation : Low in anemia of chronic disease. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: In the blood indices for anemia of chronic disease on p78, soluble transferrin receptors are:
questions.exp: Soluble transferrin receptors : Low in anemia of chronic disease. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: In the blood indices for anemia of chronic disease on p78, serum hepcidin is:
questions.exp: Hepcidin : High in anemia of chronic disease. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Match each blood index in anemia of chronic disease to its printed level — 1) Serum ferritin 2) Serum iron 3) Soluble transferrin receptors 4) Hepcidin … A) Very low B) Low C) High D) Normal / high
questions.exp: In ACD: Sr. ferritin is normal/high, Sr. iron is very low, soluble transferrin receptors are low, and hepcidin is high. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Under Sideroblastic Anemia on p78, causes are classified based on etiology into which two main groups?
questions.exp: Causes of sideroblastic anemia — Based on etiology: Inherited and Acquired. (Book p78)

questions.q: The inherited cause of sideroblastic anemia listed on p78 is ____ deficiency.
questions.exp: Inherited: ALA synthase deficiency (X-linked). (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: What is the mode of inheritance printed for ALA synthase deficiency on p78?
questions.exp: Inherited: ALA synthase deficiency (X-linked). (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Which clonal bone-marrow disorder is listed first under acquired causes of sideroblastic anemia on p78?

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Which trace-element deficiency is listed under acquired causes of sideroblastic anemia on p78? ____ deficiency.

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Which toxin/substance-use disorder is listed as the third bullet under acquired causes of sideroblastic anemia on p78?
questions.exp: Acquired causes of sideroblastic anemia: myelodysplastic syndrome, copper deficiency, alcoholism. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Which three drugs are specifically listed under acquired causes of sideroblastic anemia on p78?
questions.exp: Drugs listed under acquired sideroblastic anemia are chloramphenicol, isoniazid, and pyrazinamide. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Which heavy metal is listed at the bottom of the acquired causes of sideroblastic anemia on p78?
questions.exp: Lead is listed as the fifth bullet under acquired causes of sideroblastic anemia. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT — which of the following is NOT listed among the acquired causes of sideroblastic anemia on p78?

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: In the physiology of hemoglobin formation on p78, which two substrates and cofactor combine in the initial step?

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: In the physiology of Hb formation diagram on p78, Succinyl Co-A + Glycine + Pyridoxal phosphate are converted into ALA by the enzyme ____.
questions.exp: Succinyl Co-A + Glycine + Pyridoxal phosphate → (via ALA synthase) → ALA. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: In the p78 hemoglobin formation pathway, ALA is converted to which intermediate before combining with iron?
questions.exp: ALA → Protoporphyrin, which then combines with Iron to form Heme → Hemoglobin. (Book p78)

questions.sec: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Anemia Etiology
questions.q: In the final steps of the p78 pathway, Iron combines with Protoporphyrin to form:

Iron polymerizes into linear crystalline rods inside myeloblasts
Iron surrounds the erythroblast in the form of a ring
Iron precipitates at one pole of the mature erythrocyte as a Heinz body

questions.sec: Diagnostic Protocol for Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
questions.q: Under the 'Single' lineage arm of the p81 flowchart, what parameter is evaluated next?
questions.exp: Single lineage proceeds to Reticulocyte production index → Low vs High. (Book p81)

questions.q: Under the 'Low' Reticulocyte production index arm on p81, how does MCV divide?
questions.exp: Under Low RPI, MCV branches into Ⓝ to Low and High. (Book p81)

questions.sec: Diagnostic Protocol for Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
questions.q: In the p81 flowchart, a Normal (Ⓝ) to Low MCV leads directly to evaluation of ____.
questions.exp: Ⓝ to Low MCV → Iron indices. (Book p81)

questions.sec: Diagnostic Protocol for Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
questions.q: At the bottom of the p81 diagnostic protocol, 'Iron indices' differentiates which four conditions?
opts: Anemia of chronic disease, pure red cell aplasia, paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and IRIDA
Iron deficiency anemia, anemia of chronic disease, sideroblastic anemia and thalassemia trait
Autoimmune hemolytic anemia, G6PD deficiency, hereditary spherocytosis and sickle cell anemia
Iron deficiency anemia, megaloblastic anemia, aplastic anemia and myelodysplastic syndrome
questions.exp: Under Iron indices, the flowchart branches into: Iron deficiency anemia, Anemia of chronic disease, Sideroblastic anemia, and Thalassemia trait. (Book p81)

questions.sec: Diagnostic Protocol for Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
questions.q: TRUE or FALSE — in the p81 diagnostic flowchart, the complete sequence to reach the four microcytic/normocytic anemias is Lineage (Single) → Reticulocyte production index (Low) → MCV (Ⓝ to Low) → Iron indices.
opts: False — they sit under the Multiple-lineage branch of the protocol
True — but only when the Reticulocyte Production Index (RPI) is High
False — Iron indices are evaluated before checking MCV or RPI
True — Single lineage → Low RPI → Ⓝ to Low MCV → Iron indices is the exact flowchart pathway
questions.exp: The p81 flowchart shows Lineage (Single vs Multiple) → RPI (Low vs High) → MCV (Ⓝ to Low vs High) → Iron indices → four anemias. (Book p81)

units.title: Blood Picture & ACD Pathophysiology
units.sec: Blood Picture & Anemia of Chronic Disease Pathophysiology
units.guide:
IDA and ACD are normocytic normochromic initially; RA and miliary TB cause microcytic hypochromic ACD.
Sideroblastic anemia is dimorphic (microcytic + macrocytic); thalassemia trait is microcytic hypochromic.
Hepcidin (liver peptide) inhibits ferroportin; IL-6/activin, HFE (chr 6), hemojuvelin and Tfr2 stimulate it, while hypoxia inhibits it.

units.title: ACD Indices & Sideroblastic Etiology
units.guide:
HFE mutation causes hemochromatosis; in ACD, ferritin and hepcidin are normal/high while Sr. iron, TIBC, TSAT and sTfR are low.
Sideroblastic anemia is inherited (X-linked ALA synthase deficiency) or acquired (MDS, Cu deficiency, alcohol, chloramphenicol/INH/PZA, lead).
Normal heme synthesis proceeds from Succinyl Co-A + Glycine + B6 (via ALA synthase) → ALA → Protoporphyrin + Fe → Heme → Hb.

units.title: Sideroblastic Pathogenesis & Thalassemia
units.guide:
ALA synthase deficiency leaves unbound iron around the erythroblast nucleus as ring sideroblasts on Prussian blue stain.
Sideroblastic investigations show dimorphic cellularity, EM Pappenheimer bodies, high Sr. iron/TSAT, normal/high ferritin and low TIBC.
Thalassemia trait (ββ⁰, ββ⁺) has one normal and one defective β gene, absent ineffective erythropoiesis, and normal iron indices.

units.title: Thalassemia Indices & Inherited IDA
units.sec: Thalassemia Investigations, Master Table & Inherited IDA
units.guide:
Thalassemia trait shows normal RDW, Mentzer index <13, rare target/stippled cells, and HbA₂ 4–8% (normal 1.5–3%).
The master table contrasts Sr. iron, ferritin, TIBC and TSAT across IDA, ACD, sideroblastic anemia and thalassemia trait.
Inherited IDA includes IRIDA (defective matriptase-2 → ↑ hepcidin), DMT-1 mutation (no endosome-to-cytoplasm transport) and atransferrinemia.

units.title: Diagnostic Protocol
units.sec: Diagnostic Protocol for Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
units.guide:
The diagnostic protocol begins with Lineage (Single vs Multiple) followed by Reticulocyte Production Index (Low vs High).
Under Single lineage and Low RPI, MCV divides into Normal-to-Low versus High.
Normal-to-Low MCV proceeds to Iron indices to separate IDA, ACD, sideroblastic anemia and thalassemia trait.
